s1.p1: Very often the number of loop iterations is unknown in advance and it depends on the fulfilment of some condition.
s1.p2: As the army saying goes, ‘dig from the fence to lunch’.
s1.p3: That is why we cannot use the iteration counter because we cannot set a limit on its value.
s1.p4: In this case, we use one of the **⟦f0⟧** or **⟦f1⟧** loop operators.
s1.p5: Syntactically, the **⟦f0⟧** operator includes three mandatory parts: the word **⟦f0⟧** itself, followed by parentheses in which the logical expression (the loop condition) will be written, and then the body of the loop enclosed in curly braces:
s1.p6: What will the engine do when faced with such an expression?
s1.p7: 1. First, it will calculate the value of the boolean expression in parentheses and convert it to a boolean type.
s1.p8: 2. If the condition is satisfied (i.e. the calculated value is ⟦f2⟧), the code inside the curly brackets will be executed (the next iteration of the loop).
s1.p9: After that the engine will return to point 1.
s1.p10: ^^This loop will not be executed once because the condition ⟦f3⟧ is not fulfilled initially, i.e. the value ⟦f4⟧ will be obtained when evaluating the expression in parentheses.^^
s1.p11: ^^The loop will sum the numbers entered by the user until the ⟦f6⟧ button is pressed in the ⟦f5⟧ modal window.^^
